channel.title: Getting Started :: Go Kure — Launcher
channel.description: Pick the route that matches how you use launcher: Command line. Install kurel, then follow the Quickstart to build your first application. Go library. Install the module, then follow the library quickstart to run the same pipeline from your program. Introduction explains the two-config-set model both routes share, and Examples lists runnable application documents.

item.title: Introduction
item.description: launcher is a Go library that translates OAM-style application documents into Kubernetes objects, and kurel is the supported command-line tool built on it. You describe an application with an OAM-style document (app.yaml) — a set of typed components (webservice, worker, cronjob, postgresql, …) decorated with traits (ingress, certificate, scaler, external-secret, …) — and kurel build resolves it into static, GitOps-ready Kubernetes manifests. The two-config-set model kurel separates what an application needs from how a cluster provides it:

item.title: Install
item.description: Release binaries Each release carries kurel for Linux on amd64 and arm64 as kurel_<version>_linux_<arch>.tar.gz, with checksums.txt, a Sigstore bundle signing it (checksums.txt.sigstore.json) and an SBOM per archive. <version> is the tag without its v. The steps below download a release and check that the go-kure release workflow signed its checksums for launcher at that release’s tag. The workflow is shared by every go-kure repository, so the certificate must also name go-kure/launcher and the tag. They then check the archive against the checksums and only then install kurel (into ~/.local/bin; use any directory on your PATH). Each step runs only if the one before it succeeded:

item.title: Library Quickstart
item.description: This page builds the objects of one application from your own Go program, with the same checks kurel build runs, in the same order. The program below is the Example in pkg/oam (ExampleTransformer_Transform), which the test suite runs, so the code and the output on this page are tested. Set up a module mkdir hello && cd hello go mod init example.com/hello go get github.com/go-kure/launcher@main Then copy the replace lines of launcher’s go.mod at that revision into your own go.mod, as Install explains. Without them the build fails.

item.title: Examples
item.description: The examples/ directory contains runnable OAM Applications and cluster profiles. Build any of them with: kurel build examples/01-webservice-minimal.yaml \ --profile examples/cluster-profiles/minimal.yaml Application examples Example Shows 01-webservice-minimal / 02-…-with-expose / 03-…-with-tls / 04-…-full webservice from minimal to full (expose, TLS, probes, volumes) 05-worker-minimal / 06-worker-with-traits background workers 07-cronjob-minimal / 08-cronjob-full scheduled jobs 09-postgresql-minimal / 10-postgresql-ha CloudNativePG databases 11-helm Helm chart via Flux 12-daemonset / 13-statefulset node daemons and stateful workloads 14-full-stack a multi-component application 15-passthrough-minimal emit an arbitrary object verbatim Cluster profiles & custom capabilities cluster-profiles/ — platform profiles (minimal, cert-manager + vault, gateway + AWS, …). custom-capability/ — extending kurel with a custom capability. See the Component Handlers, Trait Handlers and Policy Handlers references for the full set of types and their properties.
